claims.quote: She wrote like this, in longhand, the way someone who had been taught to keep a slow, retrievable record might write: deliberately and without flourish.

She did not read the book; she would not read it. There was a long, unspoken etiquette to how households kept a person’s private things: they preserved them, they did not repurpose them, they made them into things to be honoured rather than instruments to be used.
“No. Tell them I was in the garden.”

claims.quote: “Very well,” she said. Her voice rearranged itself into a smaller, practical shape. “I will tell them you were in the garden.”
